corpus.t: Assessment of Chloroquine with Dodecyl sulfate. Ionic-liquid likeness: likely: long flexible C12 chain, charge spread over a sulfate head. Safety: caution: surfactant, skin and eye irritant; excipient class but not GRAS-listed. Literature status: exact pair not found; chloroquine with the C12 carboxylate (laurate) is a room-temperature ionic liquid. Verdict: promising but check irritation.
corpus.c: Silva et al., Int J Mol Sci 2020, doi 10.3390/ijms21155334

corpus.t: Assessment of Penicillinate with [2-(Methacryloyloxy)ethyl]trimethylammonium (TMAMA). Ionic-liquid likeness: possible: ester side chain adds flexibility. Safety: poor: reactive methacrylate monomer, skin sensitiser (H317), eye irritant (H319). Literature status: exact pair not found; TMAMA with cloxacillin (also a penicillin) was made as a monomer ionic liquid for polymer conjugates. Verdict: reject as a drug salt; only meaningful inside a polymer.

Assessment of Procainamidinium with Docusate. Ionic-liquid likeness: likely: bulky, branched, very flexible (flex 16), charge spread. Safety: good: GRAS/SCOGS tier A (dioctyl sodium sulfosuccinate), used as an excipient. Literature status: exact pair not found; docusate is the classic API-IL anion (lidocaine docusate is a room-temperature ionic liquid). Verdict: strong candidate.
corpus.c: Hough et al., New J Chem 2007, 31, 1429

corpus.t: Assessment of Ciprofloxacin with Clofazimine (protonated). Ionic-liquid likeness: possible: very large but rigid (flex 2.5). Safety: both partners are drugs, so this is a dual-drug pair, not an excipient question. Literature status: exact pair not found; clofazimine salts with other acids (including 4-aminosalicylic acid) are reported. Verdict: uncertain: no measured pKa for clofazimine in our table.
corpus.c: Bodart, PhD thesis, University of Namur 2021

corpus.t: Assessment of Ampicillinate with Didecyldimethylammonium. Ionic-liquid likeness: likely: two C10 chains, flexible (flex 18). Safety: poor: biocide, corrosive, rat oral LD50 150 mg/kg. Literature status: exact pair not found; ampicillin ionic liquids with ammonium, phosphonium and pyridinium cations are reported. Verdict: reject: toxic cation.
corpus.c: Florindo et al., Int J Pharm 2013, 456(2); LD50 from IUPAC/AERU pesticide database

corpus.t: Assessment of Mefenamate with Dioctadecyldimethylammonium. Ionic-liquid likeness: likely: two C18 chains, very flexible (flex 34). Safety: poor: same quaternary surfactant class as the biocide above; not on any safety list. Literature status: exact pair not found. Verdict: reject: toxic class.

Assessment of Oxybuprocaine with Docusate. Ionic-liquid likeness: likely: bulky, branched, very flexible (flex 16). Safety: good: GRAS/SCOGS tier A, used as an excipient. Literature status: exact pair not found; docusate forms room-temperature API-ILs with local anaesthetics (lidocaine docusate). Verdict: strong candidate.
corpus.c: Hough et al., New J Chem 2007, 31, 1429

corpus.t: Assessment of Meclofenamate with Cholinium. Ionic-liquid likeness: possible: choline is small and rigid, so the salt may stay solid. Safety: good: choline chloride and bitartrate are GRAS/SCOGS listed (tier B). Literature status: ALREADY PUBLISHED: a 1:1 choline meclofenamate crystal structure exists (a hydrated crystalline solid, not a liquid). Verdict: model was right; it is a salt but not an ionic liquid.
corpus.c: Dhanaraj and Vijayan, Biochim Biophys Acta 1987, 924, 135

corpus.t: Assessment of Mepacrine with Dodecyl sulfate. Ionic-liquid likeness: likely: long flexible C12 chain. Safety: caution: surfactant, irritant. Literature status: exact pair not found; same reasoning as chloroquine, which is a close analogue drug. Verdict: promising but check irritation.

Assessment of Loxoprofenate with Cholinium. Ionic-liquid likeness: possible: choline is small and rigid. Safety: good: choline salts GRAS/SCOGS listed (tier B). Literature status: exact pair not found; loxoprofen does form ionic liquids with matrine, and choline forms them with other NSAIDs (ketoprofen, naproxen). Verdict: reasonable candidate.
corpus.c: Ting et al., RSC Adv 2025, 15, 14632; Araujo et al. 2018

corpus.t: Assessment of Tolfenamate with Cholinium. Ionic-liquid likeness: possible: choline is small and rigid. Safety: good: choline salts GRAS/SCOGS listed (tier B). Literature status: exact pair not found; tolfenamate ionic liquids with cationic lipoamino acids are reported (one was a solid at 147 C, two were semi-solids). Verdict: reasonable candidate.

Assessment of 4-Aminosalicylate with N-(2 3-Epoxypropyl)-N-methyl-2-oxopyrrolidinium. Ionic-liquid likeness: possible. Safety: reject: carries an epoxide (glycidyl) group; glycidol is IARC Group 2A, a direct alkylating agent and mutagen. Literature status: exact pair not found. Verdict: reject: alkylating group.

Assessment of Pefloxacin with Docusate. Ionic-liquid likeness: likely: bulky, branched, very flexible. Safety: good: GRAS/SCOGS tier A. Literature status: exact pair not found; docusate API-ILs are known. Verdict: strong candidate.
corpus.c: Hough et al., New J Chem 2007, 31, 1429

corpus.t: Assessment of Sulfathiazolate with Tetrabutylphosphonium. Ionic-liquid likeness: likely: bulky and flexible, but highly symmetric (symmetry 24) which raises the melting point. Safety: poor: research-only, not pharma-acceptable. Literature status: exact pair not found; tetrabutylphosphonium with gliclazide (a sulfonylurea) is a room-temperature ionic liquid. Verdict: chemistry works but the cation is not usable in a medicine.
